body:
In Basic Inputs → Additional Geometry → Modify Here → Member Properties → Girder Details, the Cross Section and Side View buttons are displayed in grey.

However, grey is consistently used throughout the application to indicate non-editable or disabled controls. Since these buttons are editable/clickable, using the same grey color is misleading and creates an inconsistent user experience.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1.  Open Basic Inputs.
2.  Go to Additional Geometry.
3.  Click Modify Here.
4.  Navigate to Member Properties → Girder Details.
5.  Observe the Cross Section and Side View buttons.

**Current Behavior:**
The Cross Section and Side View buttons are displayed in grey, which is the same color used for disabled/non-editable controls.
**Expected Behavior:**
The Cross Section and Side View buttons should use the green or standard active/editable color instead of grey, so users can easily distinguish them from disabled controls.
title: Basic Inputs > Additional Geometry > Modify Here > Member Properties > Girder Details - Cross Section and Side View use disabled (grey) color despite being editable

body: **Description** In Basic Inputs → Additional Geometry → Modify Here → Member Properties → Girder Details, the position of the "Apply Changes" button is inconsistent depending on the selected girder. When Girder 1 or Girder 4 (Exterior Girders) is selected, the "Apply changes to exterior girders" button is placed immediately below the Total Span (m) field. However, when Girder 2 or Girder 3 (Interior Girders) is selected, the "Apply changes to interior girders" button is positioned noticeably lower, leaving unnecessary vertical spacing. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Open Basic Inputs. 2. Go to Additional Geometry. 3. Click Modify Here. 4. Navigate to Member Properties → Girder Details. 5. Select Girder 1 or Girder 4 and observe the position of the "Apply changes to exterior girders" button. 6. Now select Girder 2 or Girder 3 and observe the position of the "Apply changes to interior girders" button. **Current Behavior** - The Apply Changes button is positioned differently for exterior and interior girders. - Interior girders display additional vertical spacing between the Total Span (m) field and the button. **Expected Behavior** - The Apply Changes button should maintain a consistent position and spacing relative to the Total Span (m) field for all girder selections.
title: Basic Inputs > Additional Geometry > Modify Here > Member Properties > Girder Details - Inconsistent alignment of "Apply Changes" button in Girder Overview

body: **Description** In the Transverse Member Design window under the Cross Bracing tab, changing the Select Girder option to G2–G3 does not update the CAD preview. Although the selected girder pair changes in the dropdown, the CAD diagram continues to display the previous girder arrangement instead of reflecting the selected girder pair. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Open Transverse Member Design. 2. Navigate to the Cross Bracing tab. 3. Change Select Girder to G2–G3. 4. Observe the CAD preview. **Current Behavior** - The selected girder pair changes to G2–G3 in the dropdown. - The CAD preview does not update and continues to display the previous girder configuration. **Expected Behavior** - The CAD preview should refresh automatically and display the cross-bracing configuration corresponding to the selected girder pair (G2–G3).
title: Output Dock > Transverse Member Design > Cross Bracing - CAD preview does not update when selecting girder G2–G3

body: **Description** The values displayed in Transverse Member Design → Cross Bracing do not match the values configured in Basic Inputs → Additional Geometry → → Member Properties → Cross-Bracing Details. After saving the cross-bracing inputs, the output dock continues to display different (possibly default or previously stored) values instead of the user-configured values. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Open Basic Inputs. 2. Go to Design Type 3. Choose Custom 4. click Design 5. Go to the Output Dock 6. open Transverse Design 7. Navigate to Member Properties → Cross-Bracing Details. 8. Configure the cross-bracing properties and click Save. 9. Open Transverse Member Design → Cross Bracing. 10. Compare the displayed values with the configured inputs. **Current Behavior** The values shown in the output dock do not match the user-defined inputs. For example: - Type of Bracing differs. - Bracing Section Type differs. - Bracing Section Designation differs. - Top Chord Section Type/Designation differs. - Bottom Chord Section Type/Designation differs. - Spacing differs. - Other related properties may also be inconsistent. **Expected Behavior** The output dock should accurately reflect all values configured in Additional Geometry → Member Properties → Cross-Bracing Details after the inputs are saved.
title: Output Dock > Transverse Member Design > Cross-bracing > Sections Inputs - Cross-Bracing output displays incorrect values instead of the configured Additional Geometry inputs

body:
**Description**

The application uses a green highlight to indicate active or interactive elements, such as Basic Inputs, Additional Inputs, and other navigation tabs. However, the menu bar (File, Graphics, Database, Help) and the right-side toolbar (e.g., Input Dock, Output Dock, Log Window, and other dock options) do not provide similar visual highlighting.
This results in an inconsistent user interface, making these controls appear visually disconnected from the rest of the application.

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Launch the application.
2. Observe the highlighting behavior of Basic Inputs, Additional Inputs, and other tabs.
3. Compare it with the menu bar (File, Graphics, Database, Help) and the right-side toolbar (Input Dock, Output Dock, Log Window, etc.).

**Current Behavior**

- Basic Inputs, Additional Inputs, and navigation tabs use the application's green highlight theme.
- The menu bar and right-side toolbar do not provide consistent visual highlighting or active-state indication.

**Expected Behavior**

- The menu bar and right-side toolbar should follow the same visual design language as the rest of the application.
- Active or selected menu items and dock options should provide consistent highlighting or visual feedback.
title: Main Window - Menu bar and right-side toolbar lack consistent highlight behavior with the application UI

body: **Description** The dropdown menus in different parts of the application use inconsistent hover/selection highlighting. For example, in Basic Inputs → Additional Geometry → Modify Here → Member Properties → Girder Details, dropdown options are highlighted in green when hovered over or selected, providing clear visual feedback. However, in ,the Input Dock/Output Dock, the dropdown menus do not consistently use the same green highlight behavior. This results in an inconsistent user experience and makes the UI appear visually inconsistent. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Open Basic Inputs → Additional Geometry → Modify Here → Member Properties → Girder Details. 2. Open the Type dropdown (or any similar dropdown). 3. Hover over the dropdown options. 4. Compare this behavior with a dropdown in the Input Dock/Output Dock (e.g., Member dropdown). **Current Behavior** - Dropdown options in Additional Inputs use the application's green hover/selection highlight. - Dropdown options in Input Dock/Output Dock do not provide the same green hover/selection highlighting. **Expected Behavior** - All dropdown menus throughout the application should use a consistent hover and selection style. - Dropdown options should display the same green highlight when hovered over or selected, matching the application's overall UI theme.
title: UI Consistency - Dropdown hover/selection highlighting is inconsistent across the application

body:
**Description**

In Additional Inputs → Typical Section Details, different bridge components are highlighted when the cursor hovers over them. For example, the Median and Footpath are highlighted, providing visual feedback that they are interactive.

However, the Railing does not highlight when the cursor is placed over it, resulting in inconsistent hover behavior across the bridge components.

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Go to Basic Inputs
2. Open Additional Inputs.
3. Navigate to Typical Section Details.
4. Move the cursor over the Median and Footpath and observe the highlighting.
5. Now move the cursor over the Railing.
6. Compare the hover behavior.

**Current Behavior**

- Median and Footpath are highlighted when hovered over.
- Railing does not display any hover highlight.

**Expected Behavior**

- If the Railing is intended to be an interactive/selectable component, it should display the same hover highlight as the other bridge components.
- If the Railing is intentionally non-interactive, this behavior should be consistent and clearly distinguished from interactive components.
title: Basic Inputs > Additional Inputs > Typical Section Details - Railing does not highlight on hover like other bridge components

body:
While testing the Cross Section and Top View CADs, I observed two issues:

### Issue 1: Cross Bracing hover

* Hover detection works for girders.
* Hover detection does not work consistently for Cross Bracing members in the Cross Section view.

### Issue 2: Unlimited zoom-out

The Bridge Plan view allows unlimited zoom-out.

After repeated clicking of the zoom-out button:

* the bridge continues shrinking indefinitely,
* after extreme minimization the zoom controls appear to behave inversely (zoom-out begins zooming in and vice versa).

## Expected Behavior

* Hover should work consistently for all CAD members.
* Zoom-out should stop at a reasonable minimum zoom level.
* Zoom controls should maintain consistent behavior.

## Environment

* Windows
* Latest OsdagBridge build
title: CAD Viewer: Hover detection inconsistency and unlimited zoom-out in Bridge Plan

body:
### Description

- In the **Analysis and Design Results Summary** dialog:
  1. **Labeling Inconsistency:** The dropdown card is titled **Member ID**, but the options populated inside it are girder numbers (e.g. **Girder 1**, **Girder 2**). Since a girder is composed of multiple members/segments, this terminology is incorrect.
  2. **Details Tab Fails to Update:** Changing the selected girder/member dropdown does not update any of the fields or previews in the **Details** tab. The geometry/dimension fields, section properties, stiffener tables, and **Stiffener CAD** preview inside the **Details** tab remain completely static and display the layout of the first girder/member (**G1M1**) only.

- (Note: The **Analysis Results** plots and the **Design Check** equations do refresh correctly when selections change, but the **Details** tab lacks any update mechanism.)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the **Analysis and Design Results Summary** dialog from the **Output Dock**.
2. Look at the first dropdown card under **Member ID**. Note that the options are named **Girder 1**, **Girder 2**, etc.
3. Select the **Details** tab.
4. Change the dropdown selection from **Girder 1** to **Girder 2**.
5. Observe the property fields and the **Stiffener CAD** preview in the **Details** tab.

### Current Behavior

- The **Member ID** dropdown shows girder names.
- The text fields, property values, and **Stiffener CAD** preview inside the **Details** tab do not update and continue to show properties for the first girder only.
title: Output Dock > Results Summary > Dialog fields, Stiffener CAD, and   results do not update when switching Member IDs or Load Cases

body:
### Generate Results Table Dialog Uses Hardcoded Member and Load Case Lists

- **Description:** In the **Generate Results Table** dialog, the **Member** and **Load Case** dropdowns are hardcoded to fixed placeholder values instead of reflecting the active bridge model.

  - The **Member** dropdown is permanently fixed to **"Girder 1"** through **"Girder 4"**, regardless of the actual number of girders in the current bridge design.
  - The **Load Case** dropdown is permanently fixed to a static list of nine load cases (such as **"Dead Load"**, **"Live Load"**, etc.), ignoring any custom load cases or load combinations defined by the user.

- **Steps to Reproduce:**
  1. Run a bridge design with a custom number of girders (for example, **2** or **6** girders) or custom load combinations.
  2. Open the **Generate Results Table** dialog.
  3. Click the **Member** and **Load Case** dropdowns.

- **Current Behavior:**
  - The **Member** dropdown always displays the fixed list: **All Girders**, **Girder 1**, **Girder 2**, **Girder 3**, and **Girder 4**.
  - The **Load Case** dropdown always displays the same fixed set of nine options.
  - Changing either selection has no effect and does not filter the results table or the exported Excel files.
title: Generate Results Table > Member and load case dropdowns - Options   are hardcoded to fixed values

Description
The CAD model tooltip for the cross bracing does not correctly reflect the values specified in Additional Inputs → Member Properties → Cross-Bracing Details. Additionally, the tooltip format is not member-specific, making it difficult to distinguish between different bridge members.

Steps to Reproduce
1.Open the Bridge module.
2.Navigate to Additional Inputs → Member Properties → Cross-Bracing Details.
3.Select the cross-bracing section as Channel (JC 100).
4.Set the spacing to 10.0 m.
5.Save the inputs and run the design.

Actual Behavior

The tooltip uses the same generic information format for different structural members.
Expected Behavior

The tooltip should be member-specific. For example:
Cross Bracing: Display cross-bracing section and spacing.
Top Chord: Display top chord section and relevant properties.
Bottom Chord: Display bottom chord section and relevant properties.

This will make it easier for users to identify bridge members directly from the CAD model.

body:
Description

The units displayed in generate results table→ Girder Section Properties are inconsistent with those shown in the generated report.

The report displays section dimensions in millimetres (mm), whereas the exported results display the values in metres (m) while the unit is still labeled as mm. In addition, the exported values are rounded to two decimal places, causing different section dimensions to appear identical.

Steps to Reproduce
1.Design a bridge girder.
2.Generate the design report.
3.Generate results table.
4.Compare the values under Girder Section Properties in the report and table.

Actual Behavior
The report displays dimensions in mm.
The exported results display values in m, but the unit is labeled as mm.

Due to rounding to two decimal places:
14 mm is displayed as 0.01 m
8 mm is also displayed as 0.01 m
This results in loss of dimensional accuracy and inconsistency between the report and exported results.

Expected Behavior
The units should be consistent between the report and tabl.
If dimensions are exported in metres, the unit should be correctly labeled as m.
Alternatively, export the dimensions in millimetres to match the report.

If metres are retained, increase the displayed precision (e.g., three or four decimal places) so that different dimensions remain distinguishable.
title: Inconsistent units and loss of precision in generate results table – Girder Section Properties

body:
Description

The notation used for the Strength Limit State (Flexure) check is inconsistent between the GUI and the generated report.
In the report, the flexural check follows the IRC:22 notation:

Applied Moment: Mu
Design Moment Capacity: Md
	​
Check:  Mu≤Md
Utilization Ratio: Mu/Md
	​
However, the GUI in design check displays:

Applied Moment: Md
Design Resistance: Mr
	​
Check: Md≤Mr
Utilization Ratio: Md/Mr
	​
Although both approaches yield the correct utilization ratio, the notation differs between the GUI and the report, making it difficult for users to correlate the displayed values and verify the calculations.

Expected Behavior

Use consistent notation across both the GUI and the report. Since the report follows the IRC:22 convention, the GUI should also use:

Applied Moment: Mu
Design Moment Capacity: Md
Check: Mu≤Md
Utilization Ratio: Mu/Md
	​

Alternatively, if a different notation is intentionally adopted in the GUI, the same notation should be used consistently in the report, along with clear definitions of all symbols.

	​
title: Inconsistent notation for Strength Limit State (Flexure) check between GUI and report

body: Description Issue The equation displayed in the Design Check → Strength Limit State (Flexure) section does not represent the actual calculation implemented in the software. The GUI currently displays the design moment capacity as: ​ However, the source code implements the moment capacity calculation according to IRC:22-2015 Clause 603.3.1 using the Annexure-I Plastic Neutral Axis (PNA)-based composite section method. Therefore, the displayed equation is only a simplified representation and does not reflect the actual calculation performed. This makes it difficult for users to independently verify the design results, as the displayed equation cannot reproduce the reported moment capacity. Additionally, the report does not provide the intermediate calculations involved in determining the moment capacity, such as: Plastic Neutral Axis (PNA) location Compressive and tensile force calculations Lever arm Plastic moment calculation Final design moment capacity Without these intermediate steps, the reported moment capacity cannot be independently verified. Expected Behavior Update the displayed equation so that it reflects the actual IRC:22 Annexure-I composite section formulation used in the software. If the displayed equation is intended to be schematic, clearly indicate that the actual calculation follows the IRC:22 composite beam provisions. Include a dedicated section in the report showing the complete moment capacity calculation, including intermediate steps such as: Plastic Neutral Axis (PNA) determination Force equilibrium Lever arm calculation Plastic moment calculation Final design moment capacity Reference IRC:22-2015 Clause 603.3.1 IRC:22-2015 Annexure-I (Composite Section Method) This enhancement will improve transparency and allow users to independently verify the moment capacity calculation
title: Design Check (Strength Limit State – Flexure): Displayed moment capacity equation is inconsistent with IRC 22 implementation

body: Description Issue The applied bending moment reported in the Design Report is not consistent with the value displayed in the Analysis Results for the same member and selected load combination. For Girder G1 with Envelope ULS: Analysis Results Maximum Bending Moment (Mz) = 2221.22 kN·m Design Report Applied Moment (Mu) = 2661.50 kN·m Expected Behavior The applied moment used in the Design Check and Design Report should be directly traceable to the Analysis Results. This will allow users to independently verify the reported design values and maintain consistency between the Analysis Results and the Design Report.

body: Location Output Dock →analysis and design result summary →Design Check → Resistance to Longitudinal and Transverse Shear Issue The displayed equation for shear connector resistance (Qᵤ) is mathematically incorrect. The partial safety factor (γₘ) should appear in the denominator of both terms in the equation, but the current formula does not represent this correctly. Expected Behavior Display the correct equation with the partial safety factor γₘ applied in the denominator of both terms, in accordance with the design code. Suggestion Update the displayed formula so that it accurately represents the design equation used in the calculations and avoids misleading users during verification.
title: Shear Connector Resistance (Qᵤ) equation is displayed incorrectly in the design check

body:
Location

Report → Table5.16 Transverse Shear and Detailing Checks

Issue

The report does not include the detailed calculation for longitudinal shear demand (Vₗ) as per IRC 22. Intermediate calculation parameters such as vertical shear (V), transformed concrete area (Aₑc), centroid distance (Y), transformed moment of inertia (I), and the contributions from individual load cases are not shown.

As a result, users cannot independently verify the reported value of Vₗ.

Expected Behavior

The report should provide a step-by-step calculation for longitudinal shear demand (Vₗ), including:

Vertical shear (V)
Transformed concrete area (Aₑc)
Centroid distance (Y)
Transformed moment of inertia (I)
Individual load-case contributions (where applicable)
Formula substitutions and final calculation as per IRC 22
Suggestion

Include all intermediate calculation steps and parameter substitutions in the report so that users can independently verify the computed longitudinal shear demand in accordance with IRC 22.
title: Report: Detailed calculation for longitudinal shear demand (Vₗ) is missing

body:
Location

Report / Output Dock → Stress Limitation

Issue

The displayed stress calculation cannot be independently verified using the information provided in the report.

The report displays the formula:

σ = Md / Z

and reports a stress value of σ = 4.67 MPa.

However, using the Elastic Section Modulus provided in the report (Z = 6597.17 cm³) and the displayed design moment (Md = 38.80 kN·m), the calculated stress is 5.88 MPa, which does not match the reported value of 4.67 MPa.

This indicates that either:

a different section modulus (e.g., plastic section modulus) is being used in the calculation but is not identified, or
the displayed formula or reported value is incorrect.

As a result, users cannot independently verify the reported stress value.

Expected Behavior

The report should clearly specify the section modulus used in the stress calculation (e.g., elastic or plastic) and ensure that the displayed formula, input values, and reported stress are consistent.

Suggestion

Update the report to explicitly indicate the section property used in the stress calculation or correct the displayed formula/value so that users can independently verify the reported stress.
title: Report / Output Dock → Stress Limitation: Displayed stress calculation cannot be independently verified as the final value of stress is appearing to be wrong with the given values.

body: Location Output Dock → Design Check → Lateral Torsional Buckling Issue The GUI incorrectly labels the displayed value as the elastic critical moment (Mcr). For the 1.0 DL load combination, the Output Dock displays: Mcr = 2254.24 kN·m However, the report identifies 2254.24 kN·m as the Lateral Torsional Buckling Resistance (Mb), while the actual elastic critical moment (Mcr) is 10528.93 kN·m. As a result, the displayed parameter name is misleading, and the accompanying design check inequality does not correspond to the parameter actually being compared. Expected Behavior Display Mb (LTB Resistance) instead of Mcr in the Output Dock. Update the design check inequality to compare: Md < Mb instead of Md < Mcr. Ensure the parameter names are consistent between the Output Dock and the report. Suggestion Use the same terminology throughout the application and report by displaying the Lateral Torsional Buckling Resistance (Mb) in the Output Dock and reserving Mcr exclusively for the elastic critical moment.
title: Output Dock → Design Check: LTB resistance is incorrectly labeled as elastic critical moment (Mcr)

body:
Location

Report → Lateral Torsional Buckling Check

Issue

The Lateral Torsional Buckling (LTB) section of the report does not specify the governing load combination used for the design check.

In contrast, other design check sections such as Moment Capacity and Shear Capacity explicitly display the governing load combination (e.g., "Governing LC (ULS): 1.0 DL"), allowing users to identify which load case controls the design.

The absence of this information in the LTB section makes it difficult to trace and independently verify the reported design results.

Expected Behavior

The LTB report should display the governing load combination used for the design check, similar to other design check sections.

For example:

Governing LC (ULS): 1.0 DL
Governing LC (ULS): SW
Governing LC (ULS): Envelope ULS
Suggestion

body: Description Summary While testing the Deflection and Crack Control feature in the Plate Girder module, I observed two inconsistencies related to the displayed deflection criteria and reported deflection values. Issue 1: Static deflection criterion text Steps to Reproduce Open the Plate Girder module. Run the analysis. Open Girder Analysis and Design Results Summary → Design Check → Deflection and Crack Control. Switch between: 1.0 LL 1.0 DL + 1.0 LL Current Behaviour The panel always displays: Default x = 600 However: For 1.0 LL, the allowable deflection is 25.00 mm, which corresponds to L/800 for a 20 m span. For 1.0 DL + 1.0 LL, the allowable deflection is 33.33 mm, which corresponds to L/600. The calculations are correct, but the displayed text remains "Default x = 600" for both cases. Expected Behaviour The displayed criterion should match the calculation being performed. For example: 1.0 LL → Display Default x = 800 (IRC:22-2014 Clause 604.3.2) 1.0 DL + 1.0 LL → Display Default x = 600 The explanatory text should update dynamically based on the selected load combination. Issue 2: Possible inconsistency between Design Check and Report deflection values Observation For Girder G1: Design Check Load Combination: 1.0 DL + 1.0 LL Actual Deflection = 44.13 mm Generated Report (Table 5.9 – Serviceability: Deflection Checks) Total Load Deflection = 131.670 mm The relationship between these two reported values is not clear. It is unclear whether: the report is showing the governing envelope value while the Design Check shows the selected load combination, or both sections are intended to represent the same deflection result. Expected Behaviour If the Design Check and the report are intended to display different quantities, the report or UI should clearly indicate: the governing load combination, analysis case, or that the reported value is an envelope result. If they are intended to represent the same quantity, then the displayed values should be consistent.

body: **Summary** The final design results generated by the Plate Girder design are being stored in the Steel Design (KEY_SD) output dictionary. However, several Output Dock pages and UI components continue to read values from the Member Properties (KEY_MP) dictionary instead of the finalized KEY_SD values. Additionally, the units stored in KEY_SD and KEY_MP are inconsistent, resulting in incorrect or misleading values being displayed. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Add the following debug code in plategirderbridge.py file as shown in the attached image: print("\n===== GIRDER AREAS =====") for key, value in self.output_dict.items(): if "section_properties.area" in key.lower(): print(f"{key} : {value}") print("========================") 2. Run a Plate Girder design. 3. Observe the printed output. **Observations** _Issue 1_ – Final design results are stored in KEY_SD, but Output Dock uses KEY_MP The final design values are stored under: steeldesign.details.* These represent the finalized design results after analysis and design. However, several Output Dock pages and other UI components are reading values from: member_properties.* instead of the corresponding steeldesign.details.* (KEY_SD) entries. As a result, the UI may display preliminary/member-property values instead of the final design results. _Issue 2_ – Unit mismatch between KEY_MP and KEY_SD The values stored in the two dictionaries are not in the same engineering units. For example: member_properties.girder_details.section_properties.area.G1.M1 = 0.01512731 steeldesign.details.section_properties.area = 180.24 These values clearly represent different units and therefore cannot be used interchangeably. Currently, Output Dock pages referencing KEY_MP may display values that do not correspond to the finalized design values stored in KEY_SD. **Expected Behaviour** Final design outputs should consistently be read from the KEY_SD dictionary wherever design results are displayed. If KEY_MP values are intentionally used, they should be converted to the same engineering units as KEY_SD.
title: Design results are stored in KEY_SD while Output Dock uses KEY_MP, leading to inconsistent data and unit mismatch

Description

Additionally, the report does not specify:

The LTB stage used for the calculation (Construction Stage or Composite/Service Stage).
The effective unbraced length (LLTB/LLT) considered in the calculation.

As a result, users cannot independently verify the reported Mcr value or determine whether the correct LTB stage has been used.

Current Behavior

Expected Behavior
The report should include:

Complete step-by-step calculation of Mcr
The IRC:22 equation used for the calculation
All substituted parameters (E, G, Iy, It, Iw, LLTB, etc.)
The effective unbraced length used
The governing LTB stage (Construction Stage or Composite/Service Stage)

This will allow users to independently verify the reported Mcr value and confirm that the appropriate LTB stage has been considered.
title: Report: Complete Elastic Critical Moment (Mcr) Calculation and LTB Stage Are Missing

body: Description The Interaction check displayed in the Design Check panel does not represent the actual interaction equation used by the software. According to IRC:22-2015 Clause 603.3.3.3 and the generated report, when the High Shear condition is not satisfied (Vu < 0.6Vd), the interaction check is performed using only the bending term (and axial force term, if applicable). In this case, the shear interaction term is not included in the calculation. However, the Design Check GUI displays an interaction equation that implies both bending and shear terms are always considered. As a result, the displayed equation cannot reproduce the reported utilization ratio and is misleading for users attempting to verify the design. Current Behavior The Design Check panel displays a generic interaction equation that includes both bending and shear effects. For cases where Vu < 0.6Vd, the actual software calculation excludes the shear interaction term, but the displayed equation does not reflect this. Consequently, the displayed equation does not match the implemented design logic or the reported utilization ratio. Expected Behavior The Design Check GUI should display the actual interaction equation used for the selected design case. When the High Shear condition is not satisfied (Vu < 0.6Vd), the GUI should display the bending-only interaction equation (or the bending + axial interaction equation, where applicable) as specified in IRC:22-2015 Clause 603.3.3.3. The check given in the report is correct as per IRC. Alternatively, if a generic equation is intentionally shown, the GUI should clearly indicate that it is a schematic representation and specify that the shear interaction term is omitted when the High Shear condition is not satisfied.
title: Output Dock → Analysis and design result summary  → Design Check: Displayed Interaction Equation Does Not Match the Implemented Design Check

body: Description According to IRC:22-2015 Clause 603.3.3.2, the design against vertical shear is based on the nominal shear strength, which may be determined using different methods, including: Plastic Shear Resistance (Vp) Shear Buckling Resistance (Vcr) Tension Field Method (Vtf), where applicable. However, the Design Check panel displays only the plastic shear resistance equation, and performs the check as Vd≤Vr. In contrast, the generated report computes and reports the shear buckling resistance (Vcr) along with its intermediate calculations. Because the GUI displays only the plastic shear resistance while the report presents the shear buckling resistance, it is unclear which shear resistance is actually used as the governing value for the final utilization check. Consequently, users cannot independently verify the displayed shear design. Expected Behavior The Design Check panel should display the actual governing shear resistance used for the design check. If the governing resistance is based on plastic shear resistance, shear buckling resistance, or the tension field method, the GUI should clearly indicate: the governing method, the corresponding equation, the calculated resistance value, and the equation used for the final utilization ratio. This will make the Design Check panel consistent with IRC:22-2015 Clause 603.3.3.2 and improve transparency for manual verification.
title: Output Dock → Design Check: Displayed Shear Equation Does Not Represent the Governing Shear Check Defined in IRC 22

body: Issue Description In Additional Inputs → Member Properties → Stiffener Details, the user can select Intermediate Stiffener = No. The input panel then shows Intermediate Stiffener Spacing = NA, indicating that no intermediate stiffeners are included in the design configuration. However, after the design is completed: The Design Report generates Intermediate Stiffener Thickness and Intermediate Stiffener Spacing for all girders. The final bridge design indicates that intermediate stiffeners are required. Despite this, the software does not display any validation message or warning informing the user that the selected configuration is inconsistent with the design requirements. As a result, users may believe that the bridge has been successfully designed without intermediate stiffeners, while the generated design actually requires them. This creates ambiguity regarding the final design configuration and makes verification difficult. Expected Behavior If the design determines that intermediate stiffeners are required while the user has selected Intermediate Stiffener = No, the software should display a validation or warning message such as: "Intermediate stiffeners are required for the current design. The selected configuration (Intermediate Stiffener = No) is not adequate. Please enable intermediate stiffeners or allow the software to update the design automatically." Alternatively, if the software automatically introduces intermediate stiffeners during optimization, it should clearly inform the user that the original input has been overridden and update the final design configuration accordingly.

**Steps to Reproduce**

2. Navigate to the Loading tab.
3. Select Bituminous as the wearing course.
4. Observe that the density is set to 24.
5. Change the wearing course type to Custom.
6. Enter the density as 24.
7. Observe the validation warning displayed by the software.

**Expected Behavior**
The density value 24 should be accepted in Custom mode without any validation warning.

**Actual Behavior**
A validation warning is displayed when entering 24 as the density in Custom mode, even though the same value is accepted for the predefined Bituminous wearing course.
title: Custom wearing course density of 24 triggers validation warning despite matching Bituminous default density

body: **Description** When the project location is selected as Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, the location is correctly displayed in the Project Location field. However, the corresponding temperature-related values in the Additional Inputs → Loading → Temperature Load tab are not populated automatically. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Open the Plate Girder module. 2. Select Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh as the project location. 3. Open Additional Inputs. 4. Navigate to Loading → Temperature Load. 5. Observe the fields **Expected Behavior** The temperature values should be automatically populated based on the selected project location, as indicated in the help text. **Actual Behavior** Although Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh is correctly displayed as the project location, the temperature-related fields remain blank and are not auto-filled.
title: Project location values are not populated in the Temperature Load additional inputs for Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh
